Definition: from G575 and G1325; to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various applications):--deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell, yield.
BiblicalUsage: To give back, to pay over, to render what is due. The Father who sees in secret shall reward openly in Matthew 6:4, and the Son of man shall reward every man according to his works in Matthew 16:27; Revelation 22:12 says the same at the very end — behold, I come quickly, and my reward is with me. Paul turns the word the other way in Romans 12:17: recompense to no man evil for evil.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word keeps two accounts straight. God repays — openly, surely, according to works — and that is why I must not. If I take repayment into my own hands, I am collecting a debt that is not mine to collect. My part is to provide things honest in the sight of all men and leave the rendering to Him.
